name: Sunk costs and how concentrated a market gets
idea: A record of a book on sunk costs and market structure says the book holds that, although many results are delicate, some theoretical predictions stay extremely robust under reasonable changes of model and deserve a place in the search for regularities across industries. A record of a 1996 article says its empirical results back most of those predictions.
suggests: Look for the market features that matter however the model is specified, and treat any result that depends on features of this market that are hard to measure with caution.
limits: The record of the book says many results depend on market features that are hard to measure, so that some observers argue game-theory work gives little grounds for studies across industries.
competing_idea: The record of the book says it bridges the new generation of game-theoretic models of industrial organization and the traditional empirical agenda of the structure-conduct-performance paradigm.
questions: Which predictions about this market hold whatever the detailed model assumes, and which depend on details that are hard to measure?
Which features of this market can be measured, and which results lean on features that cannot?
Has the claim been tested in markets like this one, and did the tests back it?
